<!--
IS302 Group 9 Project: Predicting Life Expectancy
PART 7: INTERACTIVE DASHBOARD (flexdashboard with Shiny)

This follows R for Data Science, Chapter 29 (R Markdown formats):
  - flexdashboard builds the layout from headings
      # (level 1)  = a new page
      ## (level 2) = a new column
      ### (level 3) = a new box
  - "runtime: shiny" in the header lets us add Shiny inputs
    (sliders, menus) and the charts update when the user changes them

Files needed in the same folder as this .Rmd:
  pacific_data_cleaned.csv, comparative_data_cleaned.csv  (from our .Rmd)
  cv_performance.csv                                      (from our .Rmd)
  pacific_data_raw.csv, comparative_data_raw.csv          (the raw data)

To run it: open this file in RStudio and click "Run Document".
-->

```{r global, include = FALSE}
# This chunk runs once, when the dashboard starts.
# It loads the packages, reads the data and builds the models.
library(flexdashboard)  # dashboard layout (R4DS Chapter 29)
library(shiny)          # interactive inputs (R4DS Chapter 29)
library(dplyr)          # data wrangling
library(readr)          # read the CSV files
library(ggplot2)        # charts
library(ranger)         # random forest (Week 8 lab)

# ---- Read the data ----
income_order <- c("Low income", "Lower middle income",
                  "Upper middle income", "High income")

# Read the cleaned data and add log(TB + 1), the same as in our EDA
read_clean <- function(file, name) {
  read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(log_tb  = log(tb_incidence + 1),
           dataset = name,
           income_level = factor(income_level, levels = income_order))
}

pacific     <- read_clean("pacific_data_cleaned.csv", "Pacific") %>% droplevels()
comparative <- read_clean("comparative_data_cleaned.csv", "Comparative") %>% droplevels()

# Both datasets together, for the charts that compare them
both_cols <- c("country_name", "year", "life_expectancy", "tb_incidence", "log_tb",
               "health_expenditure_pct_gdp", "immunization_measles",
               "fertility_rate", "income_level", "dataset")
both <- bind_rows(select(pacific, all_of(both_cols)),
                  select(comparative, all_of(both_cols))) %>%
  mutate(income_level = factor(income_level, levels = income_order))

# Raw data, only used for the Data gaps page
pacific_raw     <- read_csv("pacific_data_raw.csv", na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "-999"),
                            guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = FALSE)
comparative_raw <- read_csv("comparative_data_raw.csv", na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "-999"),
                            guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Nice names for the variables, shown in the menus
var_names <- c("TB incidence (per 100,000)"         = "tb_incidence",
               "log(TB + 1)"                        = "log_tb",
               "Health spending (% of GDP)"         = "health_expenditure_pct_gdp",
               "Measles vaccination (%)"            = "immunization_measles",
               "Fertility rate (births per woman)"  = "fertility_rate")

# Colours, the same as in our EDA
col_pac <- "#1b6ca8"
col_cmp <- "#c8531e"
dataset_colours <- c("Pacific" = col_pac, "Comparative" = col_cmp)

# ---- Build the models (the same models as in Part 4) ----
model_formula <- life_expectancy ~ log_tb + health_expenditure_pct_gdp +
  immunization_measles + fertility_rate + income_level

lm_pacific     <- lm(model_formula, data = pacific)
lm_comparative <- lm(model_formula, data = comparative)

set.seed(314)
rf_pacific <- ranger(model_formula, data = pacific, num.trees = 500,
                     importance = "impurity")
set.seed(314)
rf_comparative <- ranger(model_formula, data = comparative, num.trees = 500,
                         importance = "impurity")

# Cross-validation results from our main .Rmd (the cv-performance chunk saves them)
cv_performance <- read_csv("cv_performance.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(Test = factor(Test, levels = c("In-sample (training rows)",
                                        "Random 10-fold CV", "CV by country")),
         Dataset = factor(Dataset, levels = c("Pacific", "Comparative")))

# ---- Data gaps (from the raw data) ----
data_gaps <- tibble(
  variable    = names(pacific_raw),
  pacific     = colMeans(is.na(pacific_raw)) * 100,
  comparative = colMeans(is.na(comparative_raw[names(pacific_raw)])) * 100
) %>%
  mutate(gap = pacific - comparative) %>%
  filter(gap >= 20) %>%
  arrange(desc(gap))

dataset_table <- tibble(
  ` ` = c("Rows before cleaning", "Rows after cleaning", "Rows kept (%)",
          "Countries before cleaning", "Countries after cleaning", "Years"),
  Pacific = c(nrow(pacific_raw), nrow(pacific),
              round(nrow(pacific) / nrow(pacific_raw) * 100, 1),
              n_distinct(pacific_raw$country_name), n_distinct(pacific$country_name),
              paste(range(pacific$year), collapse = " to ")),
  Comparative = c(nrow(comparative_raw), nrow(comparative),
                  round(nrow(comparative) / nrow(comparative_raw) * 100, 1),
                  n_distinct(comparative_raw$country_name), n_distinct(comparative$country_name),
                  paste(range(comparative$year), collapse = " to "))
)
```

About
=====================================

Column {data-width=600}
-------------------------------------

### What is this dashboard?

**Predicting Life Expectancy in Pacific Island Countries**
IS302 Data Analytics, Group 9, University of the South Pacific

This dashboard lets you explore what is linked to life expectancy in Pacific Island countries, and compare them with the rest of the world.

**Research questions**

1. Is TB incidence linked to life expectancy?
2. Is health spending (% of GDP) linked to life expectancy?

**How to use it**

- **Explore data:** pick a variable and a chart, then filter.
- **Pacific trends:** see how each Pacific country changed over time.
- **Model results:** see how well each model predicts, and what it found.
- **Predict:** enter your own values to get a predicted life expectancy.
- **Data gaps:** see what data the Pacific is missing.

Column {data-width=400}
-------------------------------------

### Pacific rows

```{r}
valueBox(nrow(pacific), caption = paste("Pacific rows from",
         n_distinct(pacific$country_name), "countries"), color = col_pac)
```

### Comparative rows

```{r}
valueBox(nrow(comparative), caption = paste("Comparative rows from",
         n_distinct(comparative$country_name), "countries"), color = col_cmp)
```

### Data sources

World Bank health indicators and SPC National Minimum Development Indicators (NMDI) from the Pacific Data Hub. The dashboard is built with flexdashboard and Shiny, as shown in R for Data Science, Chapter 29.

Explore data
=====================================

Column {.sidebar}
-------------------------------------

```{r}
# Shiny inputs (R4DS 29.7.2): the charts on this page use input$...
radioButtons("explore_dataset", "Dataset",
             choices = c("Both", "Pacific", "Comparative"), selected = "Both")

selectInput("explore_var", "Variable", choices = var_names, selected = "log_tb")

radioButtons("explore_chart", "Chart",
             choices = c("Scatterplot with life expectancy" = "scatter",
                         "Histogram" = "hist",
                         "Boxplot by income level" = "box"))

checkboxGroupInput("explore_income", "Income level",
                   choices = income_order, selected = income_order)

sliderInput("explore_years", "Years", min = 2000, max = 2024,
            value = c(2000, 2024), sep = "")
```

Column
-------------------------------------

### Chart

```{r}
# The data after the filters are applied. It updates when an input changes.
explore_data <- reactive({
  d <- both %>%
    filter(income_level %in% input$explore_income,
           year >= input$explore_years[1], year <= input$explore_years[2])
  if (input$explore_dataset != "Both") d <- filter(d, dataset == input$explore_dataset)
  d
})

renderPlot({
  d <- explore_data()
  validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No data for this selection. Try other filters."))
  x_label <- names(var_names)[var_names == input$explore_var]

  if (input$explore_chart == "scatter") {
    # Put the Pacific rows last, so their dots are drawn on top
    d <- arrange(d, dataset == "Pacific")
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[input$explore_var]], y = life_expectancy)) +
      geom_point(aes(colour = dataset), alpha = 0.3) +
      # Black trend lines: solid for Pacific, dashed for Comparative
      geom_smooth(aes(linetype = dataset), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
                  se = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = dataset_colours) +
      scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Pacific" = "solid", "Comparative" = "dashed")) +
      labs(x = x_label, y = "Life expectancy (years)",
           colour = "Dataset (dots)", linetype = "Trend line") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
  } else if (input$explore_chart == "hist") {
    ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[input$explore_var]], fill = dataset)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colours) +
      labs(x = x_label, y = "Count", fill = "Dataset") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
  } else {
    ggplot(d, aes(x = income_level, y = .data[[input$explore_var]], fill = dataset)) +
      geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colours) +
      labs(x = "Income level", y = x_label, fill = "Dataset") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
  }
})
```

### Summary of the selected data {data-height=200}

```{r}
renderTable({
  d <- explore_data()
  validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, ""))
  d %>%
    group_by(Dataset = dataset) %>%
    summarise(Rows = n(),
              Countries = n_distinct(country_name),
              Mean = mean(.data[[input$explore_var]]),
              Median = median(.data[[input$explore_var]]),
              Min = min(.data[[input$explore_var]]),
              Max = max(.data[[input$explore_var]]),
              `Correlation with life expectancy` =
                cor(.data[[input$explore_var]], life_expectancy),
              .groups = "drop")
}, digits = 2)
```

Column
-------------------------------------

### Over time

```{r}
renderPlot({
  validate(need(length(input$trend_countries) > 0, "Pick at least one country."))
  d <- filter(pacific, country_name %in% input$trend_countries)
  y_label <- c(life_expectancy = "Life expectancy (years)",
               tb_incidence = "TB incidence (per 100,000)",
               health_expenditure_pct_gdp = "Health spending (% of GDP)")[input$trend_var]

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = year, y = .data[[input$trend_var]], colour = country_name)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point() +
    labs(x = "Year", y = y_label, colour = "Country") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

  if (input$trend_world) {
    world_avg <- comparative %>%
      group_by(year) %>%
      summarise(value = mean(.data[[input$trend_var]]), .groups = "drop")
    p <- p + geom_line(data = world_avg, aes(x = year, y = value),
                       inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black",
                       linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
      labs(caption = "Dashed black line = average of the rest of the world")
  }
  p
})
```

Model results
=====================================

Column {.sidebar}
-------------------------------------

```{r}
radioButtons("model_test", "How the models were tested",
             choices = c("Random 10-fold CV", "CV by country",
                         "In-sample (training rows)"),
             selected = "Random 10-fold CV")

radioButtons("model_metric", "Measure",
             choices = c("R-squared (higher is better)" = "Rsquared",
                         "RMSE in years (lower is better)" = "RMSE",
                         "MAE in years (lower is better)" = "MAE"))

radioButtons("model_dataset", "Dataset for the model details",
             choices = c("Pacific", "Comparative"))
```

**Random 10-fold CV:** each row is predicted by a model that did not learn from it.

**CV by country:** each country is predicted by a model that never saw that country. This is the hardest test.

**In-sample:** the model predicts the rows it learned from, so it looks better than it really is.

Column
-------------------------------------

### How well each model predicts life expectancy

```{r}
renderPlot({
  d <- filter(cv_performance, Test == input$model_test)
  y_label <- c(Rsquared = "R-squared", RMSE = "RMSE (years)",
               MAE = "MAE (years)")[input$model_metric]

  ggplot(d, aes(x = Dataset, y = .data[[input$model_metric]], fill = Model)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(.data[[input$model_metric]], 2)),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Linear regression" = "grey60",
                                 "Random forest" = "#2a9d8f")) +
    labs(x = "", y = y_label, fill = "Model", title = input$model_test) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
})
```

### All results {data-height=300}

```{r}
renderTable({
  cv_performance %>%
    arrange(Dataset, Test, Model) %>%
    mutate(Dataset = as.character(Dataset), Test = as.character(Test)) %>%
    rename(`RMSE (years)` = RMSE, `MAE (years)` = MAE, `R-squared` = Rsquared)
}, digits = 2)
```

Column
-------------------------------------

### Linear regression: effect of each predictor

```{r}
renderTable({
  fit <- if (input$model_dataset == "Pacific") lm_pacific else lm_comparative
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  tibble(Predictor = rownames(s),
         `Effect (years)` = s[, 1],
         `p value` = ifelse(s[, 4] < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", s[, 4])),
         Significant = ifelse(s[, 4] < 0.05, "Yes", "No")) %>%
    filter(Predictor != "(Intercept)")
}, digits = 3)
```

### Random forest: which predictors matter most

```{r}
renderPlot({
  fit <- if (input$model_dataset == "Pacific") rf_pacific else rf_comparative
  imp <- fit$variable.importance
  tibble(Predictor = names(imp), Importance = imp / sum(imp) * 100) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Predictor, Importance), y = Importance)) +
    geom_col(fill = dataset_colours[input$model_dataset]) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "", y = "Importance (% of total)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
})
```

Column
-------------------------------------

### Predicted life expectancy

```{r}
renderTable({
  req(input$pred_income)
  train <- if (input$pred_dataset == "Pacific") pacific else comparative
  new_row <- tibble(log_tb = log(input$pred_tb + 1),
                    health_expenditure_pct_gdp = input$pred_health,
                    immunization_measles = input$pred_measles,
                    fertility_rate = input$pred_fertility,
                    income_level = factor(input$pred_income,
                                          levels = levels(train$income_level)))
  lm_fit <- if (input$pred_dataset == "Pacific") lm_pacific else lm_comparative
  rf_fit <- if (input$pred_dataset == "Pacific") rf_pacific else rf_comparative

  tibble(Model = c("Linear regression", "Random forest"),
         `Predicted life expectancy (years)` =
           c(predict(lm_fit, newdata = new_row),
             predict(rf_fit, data = new_row)$predictions))
}, digits = 1)
```

Try moving TB up and down to see how much the prediction changes. The two models can give different answers, because random forest can find patterns that a straight line cannot.

    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pacific" = col_pac)) +
